about: compiler/syntax: the scanner (S2a, SL5) and the tree and parser (S2b, SL6), which syntax.Parse decodes since S2d. Since S2e (the Go parser deleted) a row is killed by internal/sketch/syntax's decoder property and parse laws (TestDecodeAgreesWithView, TestFormatParseRoundTrip, TestFormatIsTheCorpusFixpoint and the scan laws), by a fixture or checker test, or, named in gap, by a law of compiler/syntax. Paths are from the repository root.

mutants.name: scan-semi-after-rparen
mutants.rule: A newline after `)` inserts a semicolon (Go's rule).
mutants.gap: killed by law SemiMasksAreTheRule (ergo test compiler/syntax), not by the agreement tests; no Go suite runs compiler/'s laws until scripts/mutants has a compiler scope (GT7, batch 22)

mutants.name: scan-end-stops-at-escaped-quote
mutants.rule: End steps over an escaped byte of a string: an escaped quote does not end it.

mutants.name: scan-raw-end-off-by-one
mutants.rule: A raw string ends after its closing backquote.

mutants.name: scan-keyword-prefix
mutants.rule: A word is a keyword only when all of it is: `fortune` is an identifier.
mutants.gap: killed by law KeywordTableIsTheRule (ergo test compiler/syntax), not by the agreement tests; no Go suite runs compiler/'s laws until scripts/mutants has a compiler scope (GT7, batch 22)

mutants.name: scan-two-byte-operator-split
mutants.from: return if c1 == '=' { Eql } else { Assign }
mutants.rule: `==` is one token, not two `=`.
mutants.gap: killed by law OpFastIsOpKind (ergo test compiler/syntax): the slow path opKind runs inside an interpolation only, which no Go test reaches; no Go suite runs compiler/'s laws until scripts/mutants has a compiler scope (GT7, batch 22)

mutants.name: scan-rune-octal-bound
mutants.rule: An octal rune escape names a byte: '\400' is not a rune literal (Go's strconv.Unquote, which oneRune reads without allocating).

mutants.name: scan-class-zero-a-letter
mutants.rule: A digit is not a letter: `0` cannot start an identifier.

mutants.name: scan-semi-mask-drops-ident
mutants.rule: A newline after an identifier inserts a semicolon.

mutants.name: scan-kwtable-swaps-two
mutants.rule: Each keyword hashes to its own kind.

mutants.name: scan-punct-comma-as-period
mutants.rule: A comma is Comma.

mutants.name: scan-path-ascii-digit-starts-element
mutants.rule: An import path element starts with a letter or `_`, not a digit.

mutants.name: scan-opfast-ignores-doubled
mutants.rule: A doubled operator byte (`<<`, `&&`, `..`) is a longer token: run's arm leaves it to opKind.

mutants.name: comments-blank-line-joins-groups
mutants.rule: A blank line between two comments ends the first one's group (go/parser).

mutants.name: failure-position-from-file-start
mutants.rule: A failure reports the line and column of its own offset.

mutants.name: tree-children-flushed-in-reverse
mutants.rule: A record keeps its children in source order.

mutants.name: tree-stack-not-cut-after-list
mutants.rule: rec cuts the stack back to the list's mark.

mutants.name: tree-rewind-keeps-extra
mutants.rule: A rewind cuts extra back to its checkpoint.
mutants.gap: killed by law ExtraTiles (ergo test compiler/syntax), not by the agreement tests; no Go suite runs compiler/'s laws until scripts/mutants has a compiler scope (GT7, batch 22)

mutants.name: view-reads-b-for-a
mutants.from: BinaryExpr{X: nid(t, a), Op: int(tok), Y: nid(t, b)}
mutants.to: BinaryExpr{X: nid(t, b), Op: int(tok), Y: nid(t, a)}
mutants.rule: View reads each operand from its own word.

mutants.name: view-none-as-row-0
mutants.rule: An optional child's 0 word is none, never row 0.

mutants.name: tree-row-gains-string
mutants.rule: A row holds no pointer (PointerFree).
mutants.gap: PointerFree needs the layout std (LAY1), not on this base: the mutant does not even compile until NewTree sets names, and no law sees a pointer field. It survives until LAY1 lands.

mutants.name: skip-without-literal
mutants.to: n == String || n == StringHead || n == LParen
mutants.rule: skip is a statement only before a string literal: skip(x) stays a call (contextual, no scanner keyword).

mutants.name: skip-end-at-keyword
mutants.from:

		return tokEnd(k, int(a))
mutants.to:
if kd == KSkipStmt {
		return tokEnd(k, tok)
mutants.rule: A skip statement ends where its reason ends.

mutants.name: columns-token-end-short
mutants.rule: A token's column carries its end, the one the scan stored: a name's or a literal's text is its whole span.

mutants.name: columns-group-last-is-first
mutants.rule: A comment group carries its last comment: a doc of several lines is every line.

mutants.name: columns-failure-unflagged
mutants.from: out = out.Append(if p.Failed { uint32(1) } else { uint32(0) })
mutants.rule: A failed parse says so in the header, so a host reports the failure, never an empty tree.

mutants.origin: wf10 STD-NOPRIV NP3b; moved to the Ergo parser at wf10 selfhost S2d
mutants.rule: grammar.md Declarations 17: entry before func is the entry type's prefix.

mutants.name: pure-clause-not-parsed
mutants.origin: wf10 STD-NOPRIV NP3a; moved to the Ergo parser at wf10 selfhost S2d
mutants.rule: grammar.md Declarations 16: pure between a parameter's name and its type is the clause.

mutants.name: builtin-target-any-name
mutants.origin: wf10 OPT4b; moved to the Ergo parser at wf10 selfhost S2d
mutants.rule: An extern target with no import path names a Go builtin.

mutants.name: try1-groups-right
mutants.origin: wf10 lang-2 TRY1; moved to the Ergo parser at wf10 selfhost S2d
mutants.rule: grammar.md Expressions 1 (q105): a try in operand position wraps its operand only; it adds no grouping.

mutants.name: orp-let-admitted
mutants.origin: wf10 FK7a; moved to the Ergo parser at wf10 selfhost S2d
mutants.rule: Alternatives stand only in a case's patterns: a let or for pattern is one shape (FK7a).

mutants.name: orp-cap-missing
mutants.origin: wf10 FK7a; moved to the Ergo parser at wf10 selfhost S2d
mutants.rule: A case expands to at most 64 patterns (FK7a).

mutants.name: tskip-scanner-reserves
mutants.origin: wf10 TSKIP; moved to the Ergo parser at wf10 selfhost S2d
mutants.rule: skip is a contextual keyword: the scanner reads it as a name, so no program loses the name.

mutants.name: tskip-call-is-skip
mutants.origin: wf10 TSKIP; moved to the Ergo parser at wf10 selfhost S2d
mutants.rule: Only skip followed directly by a string literal is the statement; skip(x) is a call.

mutants.name: parseall-every-task-parses-the-first
mutants.rule: Each file of a run is parsed: the join is each file's own parse, in file order.
mutants.gap: killed by law ParseAllIsEachParse (ergo test compiler/syntax), not by a Go suite; no Go suite runs compiler/'s laws until scripts/mutants has a compiler scope (GT7)

mutants.name: eachrun-inline-parses-the-first
mutants.from:

			out = out.Append(f(s))
mutants.to:
for s in srcs {
			out = out.Append(f(srcs[0]))
mutants.rule: The columns of a package's files are each file's own, in file order, also when the package is parsed on the caller's stack.

mutants.name: chunks-drop-the-last-file
mutants.rule: The runs cover every file: none is left out of the parse.
mutants.gap: killed by law ChunksTile (ergo test compiler/syntax); no Go suite runs compiler/'s laws until scripts/mutants has a compiler scope (GT7)

mutants.name: scan-rune-end-short
mutants.rule: The end the scan stores for a token is the token's whole span (law EndsAreStored).

mutants.name: parse-extra-not-cut-on-rewind
mutants.rule: A rewind cuts the extra pool back to the checkpoint, so the records after it start where the checkpoint's words end.

mutants.name: scan-failed-illegal-end-unset
mutants.rule: A failed scan's ILLEGAL carries its end in the ends column, which Columns copies whole.

mutants.name: scan-failed-tail-at-failure
mutants.rule: A failed scan's ILLEGAL and EOF sit at the end of the last token when that is past the failure (the Go scanner's fail).
